passage: Anirban waved his phone at Ira. "Come to the rally on Saturday, or you're not really with us," he said, and urged her to repost a furious slogan. Ira had not read the petition behind it. She read it that night, agreed with half, and shared only the part she could stand behind. At dinner she asked her mother, Madhuri, about Saturday. "No," Madhuri said at once. "Crowds turn, and I would be sick with worry." Ira felt her ears burn but said, "I hear you. Could I write letters to the council and sell bookmarks to pay for banners instead?" Madhuri thought, then nodded. In the corridor a classmate laughed. "Posters won't save a lake, Ira. Pointless." Ira took a breath and pulled out her printed figures. "Last time, forty families wrote in and the council changed the drain plan. It's slow, but it moves." That night her stomach twisted at the thought of a teacher calling the students troublemakers, or police turning up. She told Madhuri, and they read together what the rules for peaceful gatherings allowed. Being scared, Madhuri said, did not make anyone a coward.

qa.q: What did Ira offer her mother instead of going to the rally?
qa.a: She offered to write letters to the council and sell bookmarks to pay for banners.

qa.q: How did Madhuri treat Ira's wish to help differently from how Anirban pushed her?
qa.a: Anirban told Ira she was not really with them unless she came and reposted a furious slogan, while Madhuri said no to the rally but agreed to letters and bookmarks, and later read the rules with Ira and said being scared did not make anyone a coward.

qa.q: What was Ira feeling that night when she thought about teachers and police?
qa.a: She felt afraid of the consequences; her stomach twisted, and she chose to tell Madhuri.

qa.q: What could Ira do next to keep helping the cause?
qa.a: She could keep writing letters and selling bookmarks, and keep gathering facts for anyone who calls it pointless. 🙂

grounding: One teen meets peer pressure, a parent's ban, a sceptical classmate and her own fear while deciding how to take part in a cause.
